text:
Maria: heads up — after last night's kernel + driver rollout (kernel 6.4.12 + driver 535.XX) we started seeing P2P disabled across several A100 hosts in us-west-2. reporting high NCCL latency and some jobs falling back to PCIe copies.

Priya: thanks — any idea how many hosts?

Maria: initial blast shows ~12 hosts failing P2P, mostly bar1/peer access errors in dmesg. affected ones are ampere-{03..14}.usw2.

Jon: throwing logs here, short snippet: 
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=2467, ...
[  123.456790] nvpeeraccess: peer access disabled between 0000:65:00.0 and 0000:66:00.0 
[  123.456792] pci 0000:65:00.0: BAR1 region size mismatch, expected 0x40000000 got 0x10000000
```

Lee: BAR1 sizing mismatch screams kernel PCI resource allocation change or ACS/ACS-override behaviour. did rediscover the ACS patch landed in kernel-6.4.12?

Priya: we flipped the kernel config to enable the new upstream ACS quirk (per security audit) during the rollout. that might tighten PCIe isolation and break P2P.

Maria: nvidia-smi topo -m shows now: 
```
        GPU0    GPU1    GPU2
GPU0     X      SYS     SYS
GPU1    SYS      X      SYS
GPU2    SYS     SYS       X
```
no PHB/NVLink links, P2P paths all SYS.

Jon: NCCL logs: 
"NCCL WARN Call to connect failed: Unreachable (host=ampere-07)" and fallback to p2p disabled path. throughput drops ~55% on multi-node runs.

Priya: deploy-bot: rollback of kernel 6.4.12 started for tag rollout-2026-03-18 on staging and canary in us-west-2. :gear:

deploy-bot: rollout step: canary finished, detected anomalies -> paused.

Lee: request: do not continue broad rollout. we need a targeted rollback on production group A (ampere-03..ampere-14) and hold others.

Maria: agreed. what are the safety checks? any silent failures without dmesg? some hosts showed no explicit errors but P2P still blocked.

Jon: there are two failure modes: 1) explicit BAR1 mapping smaller -> driver refuses to map p2p. 2) ACS route rewrite -> PCIe enumeration hides peer capability even though BAR1 size is correct. check `lspci -vvv` for `ACS` flags and `Vendor Specific` entries.

Priya: quick command set to triage: 
```
# check BAR1 size
sudo lspci -s 65:00 -xxxx | grep -A3 "Region 1"
# check ACS
sudo lspci -s 65:00 -vv | grep -i acs -A2
# nvidia peer access
sudo nvidia-smi topo -m
```

Maria: running across ampere-05 now. output: `Region 1: Memory at f6000000 (32-bit, non-prefetchable) [size=0x10000000]` expected 0x40000000.

Lee: that's the BAR1 shrink. likely kernel changed the bridge window calculation for that root complex. could be BIOS/firmware interaction too — any FW updates applied?

Priya: no BIOS updates this week. only kernel and driver. driver 535 should handle but with new kernel the PCI resource allocation algorithm changed.

Jon: short-term plan: rollback kernel on impacted nodes, revalidate peeraccess, then run small-scale NCCL tests. medium-term: reproduce in lab with same kernel/driver and try pinned ACPI/resource settings or pass ACS override to kernel param for affected machines.

Maria: sched ops: we can't rollback all affected nodes at once, need to schedule in waves to avoid major capacity impact. impact: 12 hosts * avg 8 GPUs = 96 GPUs out of ~1200 in west = ~8% capacity loss for multi-GPU workloads.

Priya: cost note — if we keep them degraded and jobs fall back to PCIe, token costs and job runtimes increase. ops: estimate run-time CO2? jk but real cost is ~1.6x GPU-hours for multi-node jobs.

Lee: can we isolate by marking nodes with `no-p2p` taint and auto-route jobs? that avoids noisy failures. But that reduces throughput for ML customers.

Jon: added a temporary scheduler label: `gpu.p2p=disabled` for the 12 hosts so we can avoid scheduling multi-node MPI/JAX jobs on them.

Maria: update — started rolling back ampere-03..ampere-06, will monitor NCCL throughput.

Priya: note for incident report: include kernel config diff and driver package version. also include which nodes were canaries and their outputs.

Jon: experiment idea: run `setpci` to resize BAR1? risky in prod, but in lab we can try to nudge resource window.

Lee: AGREE but don't run setpci on prod. run in lab images only.

sre-oncall: do we need to open vendor ticket with NVIDIA? might be a combined kernel-driver regression.

Priya: yes, opening internal ticket and capturing /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, dmesg, lspci dumps. RMS: send to nvidia with reproducer in lab.

Maria: on ampere-03 after rollback: `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows NVLINK/PHB back, peeraccess restored. perf back to ~98% on verification run.

Lee: good. so rollback works. Plan: finish rollback for the 12 hosts overnight, keep rollout paused, and prepare reproduction lab.

Jon: I'll add kernel boot param experiment notes: `pci=realloc` vs `pci=realloc=off` and test ACS quirk toggles.

Priya: thanks team. I'll draft short postmortem and schedule a follow-up meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT.

Maria: tagging impacted clusters in infra inc tracker: INC-2026-0423.

Lee: thumbs up. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout unpaused? no — remains paused.

Maria: closing thread for now, will update when rollbacks complete.

Priya: noted — will attach logs to the ticket.
